facts.text: Over 3,400 businesses operate in Georgina, about 73% of them owner-operated without employees.
facts.evidence: There are over 3,400 businesses with and without employees operating within Georgina. About 73% of these businesses are owner operated, without employees.

facts.text: The Keswick Business Park has generated more than 250 jobs, and Milwaukee Tool announced its expansion into Georgina in 2025.
facts.evidence: The park has generated more than 250 jobs and continues to attract companies seeking relocation and expansion opportunities. In 2025, Milwaukee Tool announced its expansion into Georgina

facts.text: Georgina's three business improvement areas in Jackson's Point, Keswick and Sutton represent more than 150 storefront businesses.
facts.evidence: The municipality has three designated business improvement areas (BIAs) that offer walkable downtown shopping and dining experiences close to Lake Simcoe in Jackson's Point (est. 1992), Keswick (est. 2014) and Sutton (est. 1995), representing more than 150 storefront businesses.

facts.text: Keswick is Georgina's largest urban centre and is home to about half of the town's residents.
facts.evidence: The community of Keswick is the largest urban centre and is home to about half of the Town's residents.

meta.descriptor: a lakeside town on the south shore of Lake Simcoe in York Region
meta.fact: home to more than 3,400 businesses, most of them owner-operated

overview: Georgina had 47,642 residents in 2021, up 4.9% from 45,418 in 2016, living in 17,895 occupied homes on 287.69 square kilometres. The median household income in 2020 was $98,000, giving many households solid spending power.

Most local firms are owner-operated, and shoppers are split among Keswick, Sutton, Jackson's Point and rural hamlets along Lake Simcoe. Tourists add summer demand, so businesses need to serve both residents and seasonal visitors.
